It seems interesting and the way that it breaks expectations at breakneck pace is innovative and would take a lot of work, but the core issues of the game permeate the whole game like a moldy cheese.
1. It practically requires controllers but the default mapping for my controller (ps5 controller) is absolutely ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. It turns camera left without any button pressed, then I can hold down left trigger to turn camera right and right trigger to turn camera up and down - except that holding right trigger all the way down pauses the game.
2. Once you reach the Vivian parts of the game, there are multiple flying sections which have the most painfully floaty controls, it's miserable to move around
3. I often can't control the camera when I feel like it would help and I don't know if that's intended or if the game is just broken in that way?
4. Sometimes the game just vibrates the camera slightly in a way that makes me dizzy
5. If you do have issues with the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ controller mapping and switch to keyboard/mouse, mouse looking has been implemented to be completely abrupt so it feels horrible - needs just a tiny bit of mouse input smoothing (2 frames is generally enough) to be okay!
6. The audio is poorly balanced - this is on purpose probably so that it can break expectations better

I also think the game is at its best when it contrasts looking terrible with looking nice but only a couple screens look nice so it's mostly an offputting, jarring, confronting experience

Soda Drinker Pro is an emotional story about a boy exploring his subconscious. The mundanity, the surreality, and the repressed trauma, guided by his one comfort, soda. Moments jump from normal locations he's seen throughout life, often getting specific down to a tee, to memories abstracted from the passage of time. Some levels have a slow pace, simulating being bored in unexciting locations, and others make everyday objects and places seem gigantic, reminiscent of a child's view. The soundtrack aids greatly in the emotional impact of the story, most tracks have basic fl studio preset sounds to them, reflecting the mundanity of the level, but some tracks venture into loud, blaring notes to instill a sense of mania. 

I will not spoil any details of the individual levels for you, but I encourage you to play through all 102 main levels + the bonus levels for the full experience. Soda Drinker Pro might not be the most accessible game, but offers a wonderful heartfelt experience if you can handle the high-end graphics, and I'd reccomend it to you walking simulator enjoyers out there.

Soda Drinker Pro is a game I've come back to every now and again for years. It's been a fun game to pull out at parties and laugh at, but until January of this year, I was unaware of Vivian Clark. It's a hidden game inside of Soda Drinker Pro that is much larger and more detailed than Soda Drinker Pro. It's one of the coolest easter eggs I've ever seen in a video game. Following this, I decided to research this game as much as possible. There were a lot of missing pieces to this story though. Vivian Clark seemed to be a separate project at one point, all the levels were ideas created by donors, and the demake is a complete mystery with no way of playing the game or watching it online. With how much I've loved this game over the years and barely finding information online, I took it upon myself to compile the most detailed documentation of this game and its development. I documented everything that is currently readily available online, old web pages that have been taken down, interviews containing important questions about its development, and I also got in contact with Nathan Boehm, the creator of the demake, to properly document its history in full and upload a long play of his demake. I am making this review because if it wasn't for the Steam reviews talking about level 2, I would've never discovered Vivian Clark. So this documentary is my contribution to the community. If you are at all interested in this game's history, I'd highly recommend watching my video. I can confidently say that this is the most up-to-date and in-depth resource when finding information about these three games.

Soda Drinker Pro and its equally whimsical and humorous Vivian Clark microgame experience are extremely unique games with an outsider art appeal to their sound design, aesthetics, and environments. Both games have clunky controls, which is particularly bothersome when playing the hidden Vivian Clark microgames.

The gameplay and controls are thin, buggy, and unwieldy; which is a significant detriment to the fast paced and sometimes inscrutable microgames. The humorous and outsider art aspects of the base game are very easy to enjoy and recommend, but they don't completely make up for the other glaring issues and won't be for most people.

While I have enjoyed my experience with both parts of the game, I would not generally recommend Soda Drinker Pro. The aesthetics have to deeply resonate to make this a game worth recommending.
If you want to play this on a Steam Deck, try setting the resolution to 1280 x 800. That should fix most issues.
